zh: 昨天我们讨论过了，今天只是确认一下。
chinglish: Yesterday we discuss already, today we just confirm.
standard: We already discussed it yesterday; today we're just confirming.
notes: The time word 'yesterday' opens the sentence and does the work of the past tense.
Time first; future is implied by 'tomorrow', and 'to' is dropped (see also P07).

standard: The weather is very good today.
notes: Time first; no copula (P03) and no article (P12).
Past tense carried by 'last night', not by the verb.

standard: We have a meeting next week.

chinglish: Every day I get up early.
standard: I get up early every day.
notes: Chinese puts 'every day' at the front of the clause.

standard: I go to the office on Monday.

notes: Past from 'yesterday', not from the verb form.
Time first; no tense change on the verb.
This one actually matches English order — a happy overlap.

chinglish: Three days ago she come here.
standard: She came here three days ago.
notes: Time phrase first; verb stays base form.

standard: I don't have time right now.
notes: Time first, plus the no+verb negation pattern (P08).
'already' carries completion instead of have + past participle.

zh: 我们明天完成这项工作。

notes: 'before' implies the experience; no perfect tense needed.
'yesterday night' is a direct translation of 昨晚; English says 'last night'.
No tense or modal marking; context does the work.

standard: I've lived here for ten years.
notes: Duration with no perfect tense and no 'for'.
'already' + base verb instead of present perfect.
Same pattern: the time word is the tense.

zh: 他在这家公司工作五年了。
chinglish: He work in this company five years.
standard: He has worked at this company for five years.
notes: Duration phrase without 'for' or perfect tense.
The copula 'is' is simply absent; the adjective is the predicate.
No copula; negation with 'not' directly before the adjective.
Adjective predicate; time word at the end.

zh: 这个项目我们三家一起做。
chinglish: This project we three companies together do.
standard: Three companies are doing this project together.
notes: Topic ('this project') is announced first, then the comment.

standard: I have no solution to this problem.
notes: Topic first, then 'I have no solution'.
Topic ('that movie') fronted; the verb stays short.

standard: I like this book very much.

chinglish: The meeting tomorrow morning we have.
standard: We're having the meeting tomorrow morning.

notes: Topic 'English' fronted; comment is the whole clause.

standard: I want to ask you this question.
notes: Topic + 'I ask you'; English needs more structure.

standard: We don't go to that place.

notes: Topic fronted, then subject + verb + time.

standard: I'm going to see a movie.
We went shopping to buy clothes.

notes: This one actually works in casual English too.

standard: He went to open the door.
I'd like two pieces of bread.
notes: Measure word 'piece' carried over; no plural, no 'of'.
'of' is dropped after the measure word.
Measure word + noun, no plural or 'of'.
No plural on the measure word.
No measure word, no plural — just number + noun.
Measure word carries the counting; noun unchanged.

zh: 我们在会上讨论了这个问题。
chinglish: We discuss this problem on meeting.
standard: We discussed this problem at the meeting.
I didn't go to school today.
We have a meeting on Monday.
I'll wait for you at the door.

chinglish: He go to work by car.
standard: He goes to work by car.
The book is on the table.

notes: The classic: 'no' directly before the verb.

standard: I also want to buy one.
notes: 'also' before the verb; 'to' dropped after want.
'all' before the verb, as in Chinese.
'also' before the verb; 'too' at the end is the English habit.
Intensifier before the verb, as in Chinese.
'already' before the verb; completion via adverb (P13).
'only' works the same in both languages here.
'first' before the verb in Chinese order.

zh: 因为我生病了，所以没来。
chinglish: Because I sick, so I no come.
standard: I didn't come because I was sick.
notes: Chinese keeps both 'because' and 'so'; English uses one or the other.

zh: 因为下雨，所以我们没去。
chinglish: Because rain, so we no go.
standard: We didn't go because of the rain.

chinglish: Because no money, so I no buy.
standard: I didn't buy it because I had no money.

chinglish: Because busy, so I no reply.
standard: I didn't reply because I was busy.

zh: 因为累了，所以我很早睡。
chinglish: Because tired, so I sleep early.
standard: I went to bed early because I was tired.

chinglish: Because expensive, so I no buy.
standard: I won't buy it because it's too expensive.

zh: 因为他帮了我，所以我谢谢他。
chinglish: Because he help me, so I thank him.
standard: I thanked him because he helped me.

zh: 因为没时间，所以我们没完成。
chinglish: Because no time, so we no finish.
standard: We didn't finish because there was no time.

zh: 因为晚了，所以我不等了。
chinglish: Because late, so I no wait.
standard: I didn't wait because it was late.

zh: 因为冷，所以我多穿点衣服。
chinglish: Because cold, so I wear more clothes.
standard: I wore more clothes because it was cold.

zh: 因为她没来，所以我们等着。
chinglish: Because she no come, so we wait.
standard: We waited because she hadn't come.
notes: Both connectives; no+verb in the clause.

zh: 因为没有公交车，所以我走路。
chinglish: Because no bus, so I walk.
standard: I walked because there was no bus.

notes: Even irregular plurals flatten to the base form.
No plural; subject-verb agreement also flattens.

zh: 这家公司有 100 名员工。

standard: I saw a movie last night.
notes: No article; time word marks the past.
No article before the noun phrase.
'already' after the verb instead of have + past participle.
Past participle used alone, no auxiliary.
Base verb + 'already' instead of perfect tense.
'already' after the verb — the mirror of English.
Chinese softens with 'I think'; English prefers 'maybe/could'.

chinglish: I want ask you one thing.
standard: I'd like to ask you something.
notes: 'want ask' chains; 'one thing' is a direct translation.
'suggest no go' — the object is a bare verb.
'together' before the verb, as in Chinese.
The particle '啊' (ah) adds emphasis at the end.
'吧' (ba) is a suggestion particle — nothing in English.
'呢' (ne) softens a question; often dropped in English.

chinglish: You know ma, I no good English.
standard: You know, my English isn't great.

notes: '呢' (ne) adds a knowing tone; no copula either.
